implementation_notes: Network.framework replaces the BSD accept path on Apple platforms: NWListener with newConnectionHandler yields NWConnection objects (the handler role); NWConnection(start:to:) dials (the connector). SwiftNIO provides the same split portably—ServerBootstrap.childChannelInitializer configures a fresh handler pipeline for every accepted child, ClientBootstrap is the connector side, and ServerBootstrap.bind returns an EventLoopFuture<Channel> for the listening channel. Bridge that future to async/await only at the application boundary. NWListener requires the instance to be retained while active—a deallocated listener stops accepting silently.
pitfalls: The listener must be retained while active or acceptance stops.
NWConnection starts on a queue and must be driven through its .ready/.failed/.cancelled states; ignoring state transitions causes hangs.
SwiftNIO: initialise child channels before registration to avoid dropped reads; never write on the listening channel.

ServerBootstrap requires a compatible EventLoopGroup (for example MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup or SelectableEventLoop), not specifically MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup; verify compatibility before binding.
channelHandler context.eventLoop is the event loop the handler was registered on; do not block it with CPU-heavy work.
